name: Bonaparte's Gull
rangeDescription: Northern north america; winters to mexico and greater antilles
description: The most common small gull through most of North America, especially inland. Breeding adults have a black head, thin white eye arcs, bright red legs, light gray upperparts, and black wingtips.

name: Todd's Antwren
rangeDescription: Far eastern venezuela to the guianas and far northern brazil
description: Common antwren of mixed-species flocks in forest canopy, but sometimes found away from them; heard frequently but seldom seen. From below, note clean white underparts, long tail, and rather heavy bill.

name: White-winged Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Aral sea to lake balkhash, northeastern afghanistan, and far western china
description: Large black-and-white woodpecker; very similar to Great Spotted Woodpecker, but with a single large and rather formless white patch dominating the entire wing instead of scattered white dots and bars. Found in waterside clusters of forest, preferring poplar stands, in the largely dry and treeless expanses of Central Asia.

name: Lazuline Sabrewing
rangeDescription: Mountains of colombia, venezuela, and eastern ecuador
description: Large, distinctive hummingbird. Males have bright blue underparts with maroon tail and downcurved bill.

name: Trinidad Motmot
rangeDescription: Trinidad and tobago
description: Fantastic bird with a long, racket-tipped tail found only in Trinidad and Tobago, where it is the only motmot. No other bird in the country shares its beautiful orange, green, and blue color pattern, and the black mask, breast spot, ruby eye, and large size make it truly unforgettable.

name: Yellow-throated Cuckoo
rangeDescription: Sierra leone to southern cameroon, southwestern south sudan, western uganda, and eastern democratic republic of the congo
description: A small green-backed forest cuckoo of West and Central Africa. Males have a distinctive bright yellow throat and a brown-and-black barred belly, while females lack the yellow throat and have a brown-and-black barred face, throat, and breast.

name: Rusty-barred Owl
rangeDescription: Paraguay to southeastern brazil (minas gerais) and far northeastern argentina
description: Uniform buffy-brown owl with dark eyes. Mottled brown and white above and lightly barred on the breast.

name: Black-hooded Sunbeam
rangeDescription: Andes of western bolivia (la paz and cochabamba)
description: Unique and spectacular hummingbird of the upper humid montane forest in Bolivia. Plumage mostly black, with striking white feathers on breast and a shining blue rump.

name: Hudson's Black-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Central argentina; winters to bolivia, southwestern brazil, and southeastern peru
description: Highly migratory flycatcher that breeds in central Argentina from around September through March, then disperses north to Bolivia and Paraguay, and occasionally wanders even farther. Male is glossy black with a silvery, black-tipped bill.

name: Worm-eating Warbler
rangeDescription: Eastern usa; winters southeastern mexico to panama and greater antilles
description: A plain warbler dressed in subtle shades of olive, brown, and buff. Note black and tan stripes on head and long, sharp bill.

name: Red-fronted Parrotlet
rangeDescription: Humid foothill forest of southeastern costa rica and western panama
description: Small parrot with short square tail. Mostly green with red forehead and shoulder.

name: Española Ground-Finch
rangeDescription: Española (galapagos)
description: A large and stout-billed Galápagos finch confined to the island of Española. Identification is straightforward, since the only other finches living on Española (Small Ground-Finch and Gray Warbler-Finch) have relatively tiny bills.

name: Saipan Reed Warbler
rangeDescription: Saipan and alamagan (northern mariana islands)
description: A relatively large plain brown reed warbler with a pale throat, a yellowish face, a darker cap and tail, and an absurdly long decurved bill. Found in areas of tall dense grasses, reed marshes, and scrubby thickets up to 400 meters of elevation.

name: Kilombero Cisticola
rangeDescription: Southern tanzania (kilombero swamp)
description: A large, relatively colorful marsh cisticola. Note the rufous cap, the short white eyebrow stripe, and the pale and black bands at the tip of the tail.

name: Luzon Racquet-tail
rangeDescription: Mountains of luzon (northern philippines)
description: A medium-sized parrot of montane forest on Luzon. The two central tail feathers have extended shafts ending in a racket shape.

name: Indigo Macaw
rangeDescription: Caatinga of eastern brazil (northern bahia); on verge of extinction
description: Large, beautiful blue macaw. Note the bare yellow eyering and base of lower mandible.

name: Yellow-billed Amazon
rangeDescription: Humid forest of jamaica
description: A chunky green inhabitant of wet forests; typically found in pairs or small flocks in or near the canopy. Note this species’ yellow bill, rosy throat, and white eyering.

name: Pectoral Sandpiper
rangeDescription: Breeds arctic north america and siberia; winters to southern south america, australia
description: Beefy, medium-sized sandpiper. Brown-toned overall with yellowish legs.

name: Bornean Stubtail
rangeDescription: Mountains of northern borneo (kinabalu to liang kubung)
description: Minute, ground-dwelling warbler of Borneo’s central mountain ranges. Scurries about like a rodent in the undergrowth, where it can be difficult to see well; note bright orangish brow stripe, brown back, and gray sides.

name: Taliabu Bush Warbler
rangeDescription: Taliabu island (sula islands)
description: A recently described species endemic to the declining montane forests of Taliabu. Dark, sparrow-sized warbler with a scruffy-looking, graduated tail.
